name: Smith County, TX
findings: Smith County has 711 nonprofit organizations. 268 of them (38%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 220 organizations.
Religious organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (30% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Smith County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.
32% of the organizations offering opportunities have no identified type, so the breakdown by type is partial.

observations.title: Few education organizations list membership
observations.text: 4 education organizations here list membership. In similar places of this size, about 13 would.

confidence.text: Based on 13 organizations here; 48% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Do people here look for groups to join through education groups? Where else does that happen?

observations.title: Fewer organizations list civic or political action
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Smith County list civic or political action in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 50% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 8 organizations here; 48% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find ways to take civic or political action now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Religious organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 76 religious organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

confidence.text: Based on 76 organizations here; 48% of all organizations here have no identified type.
